title: Bank rate report
description: What one bank was offering on housing finance on one day. Rates move constantly, so a report is a dated observation rather than a fact: it is never edited, and a later reading is a new report.

bank.description: The bank's own name, as it writes it.

kind.description: A participation bank sells a profit share, not a loan at interest. The instalment arithmetic is the same, the product is not, and someone choosing on that basis must be able to see which is which.

source_url.description: The page the figures were read from, so the reading can be checked or repeated.

offers.description: Empty is a real answer: a bank that publishes no rate today is not the same as a bank nobody looked at.

monthly_rate.description: Percent per month, as Turkish banks quote it. 2.79 means 2.79%.

conditions.description: What the rate depends on — salary customer, first home, energy class, a campaign end date. A rate without its conditions is not comparable with another.

example.description: The bank's own worked example, which is what makes the real cost computable. A quoted rate prices the face amount; what matters is the rate on what the borrower actually receives, and that needs the amount, the term, the instalment and anything taken at drawdown.

upfront_interest.description: Interest taken at drawdown, so it never reaches the borrower. The whole point of a peşin faizli product.

fees.description: Every up-front charge added together — tahsis, ipotek tesis AND ekspertiz. This said 'not ekspertiz, which is a service bought either way', which is a defensible view of what a loan costs and the wrong one here: every bank that publishes both a worked example and its own yıllık maliyet oranı puts ekspertiz inside it. Akbank, Halkbank and VakıfBank all reproduce exactly with it and none reproduces without — Akbank İlk Evim 24 ay is %66,6197 against %52,8311. Excluding it would break the checksum against the bank's own figure, which is the only independent check this arithmetic has.

published_annual_cost_rate.description: The bank's own yıllık maliyet oranı, as a percentage. Recorded rather than recomputed: where it disagrees with ours, the disagreement is the interesting part.

note.description: Caveats attached to these figures — what the fees cover, what varies.

source_url.description: The page this example was copied from, when it differs from the report source.

captured_at.description: When the reading was taken, to the minute. Optional, and the reason it exists is corrections: two readings of one bank on one day are indistinguishable by date alone, so without this a mistake found the same afternoon could not supersede the morning's file.

supersedes.description: The file this reading replaces, when it is a correction. The earlier one stays on disk — append-only means the record is never silently improved, not that a mistake has to stand.

reading.description: What the figures in this report mean, in the scout's own words. Which entries stand out and why, what the trade-off is, and what NOT to read into it. It may only rest on figures recorded in this same report — an interpretation that needs a number the reader cannot see is an assertion, not a reading. It is opinion, and it is shown as opinion, separately from the measurements.
